title: Eka is worth $1.45B thanks to a physical AI model that has experts raving
slides: Why does Eka's $1.45B valuation surprise AI experts?
Its physical AI model simulates real-world physics directly
Unlike LLMs, it predicts matter behavior without training data
Engineers can now test materials virtually before building
Ask your R&D team which simulation they trust today
thread_text:
1. The $1.45B question

Investors just valued an AI company at nearly a billion and a half before most engineers could name its product. The gap between hype and proof is where the real story lives.

2. Physics, not words

Eka's model predicts how matter behaves by simulating real-world physics directly — no training corpus, no next-token guessing. It starts from equations, not examples.

3. Data is the weak point

LLMs fail on physical prediction because they memorize patterns, not laws. Eka claims its engine works on problems it has never seen, which is where simulation actually matters.

4. Virtual before physical

Engineers can now run material tests inside a model instead of a lab — compressing months of prototyping into hours. That changes who gets to build what, and how fast.

5. Trust the model?

Ask your R&D team: which simulation do they actually trust today, and what would it take to trust a new one? That answer tells you more than any valuation.
